items.title: Amateur astronomer harnesses AI to find a possible hidden exoplanet
items.excerpt: Evidence for a possible super-Earth had been lurking for years in NASA TESS data; amateur Pavel Rabtsevich found it with help from AI tools.

items.title: New 'First Proof' exam reveals how AI-powered math is a pay-to-play sport
items.excerpt: A new research-level math benchmark confirms some frontier AIs are becoming exceptional tools for mathematicians, while open-source models still struggle.

items.title: OpenAI's blockbuster Navier-Stokes proof isn't what we thought it was
items.excerpt: Rumors that OpenAI's Navier-Stokes result appropriated two mathematicians' work may have been overblown, but the episode shows how AI is reshaping credit in mathematics.

items.title: Physicists develop early warning system that predicts when an AI is about to go rogue
items.excerpt: A physics-derived formula tracks an AI model's internal 'compass needle' to flag undesirable outputs before they are produced.

items.title: OpenAI claims we've entered the AGI era — has GPT-6 Astra really demonstrated general intelligence?
items.excerpt: OpenAI says GPT-6 Astra brings humanity to the threshold of AGI, but external evaluators argue inflated lab metrics and opaque testing obscure its true reliability.

items.title: Putting Earth AI to work: Geospatial agents for our planet's biggest challenges
items.excerpt: A new technical report shows a Geospatial Reasoning agent combining domain foundation models, spatial tools and upfront planning to do planetary-scale analysis and prediction that standalone LLMs cannot.

items.title: Analyzing technical documents with Deep Review
items.excerpt: After running on 16,000+ submissions at STOC, ICML, NeurIPS and ICLR, Google's AI peer-review system Deep Review launches publicly for rigorous verification of mathematical and scientific documents.

items.title: HiRO-ACEv2: Simulating extreme weather at 3 km resolution for a fraction of the cost
items.excerpt: Ai2's ML climate emulator HiRO-ACEv2 captures extreme rain, wind and pressure events at 3 km resolution for about 1/300th the cost of the X-SHiELD physics model.

items.title: How Molmo 2's open release helped an MIT researcher rethink fish tracking
items.excerpt: MIT researcher Kai Van Brunt built Molmo2Fish on the open Molmo 2 model to track salmon in sonar footage and correct tracking errors using plain language.

items.title: Now in Nature: Retrofitting language models to operate over bytes
items.excerpt: The technique behind Ai2's byte-level Bolmo language models is now published in Nature, with new checkpoints showing it generalizes beyond Olmo to other model families.

items.title: AI reveals a hidden chemical shortcut that could turn CO2 into fuel
items.excerpt: Scientists used AI to uncover nearly 10,000 reactions in CO2-to-fuel conversion on copper catalysts, revealing pathways traditional models missed and sharply improving predictions.

items.title: AI can act exactly like a human, but we still don't think it's conscious
items.excerpt: A study finds people rate even the most responsive AI as less conscious than the least responsive human, drawing a sharp line between human and machine minds even when behavior is identical.

items.title: AI-enhanced weather model doubles predictive power two to six weeks out
items.excerpt: MIT-led researchers built a machine-learning layer that learns and corrects ECMWF forecast errors, roughly doubling subseasonal (2-6 week) skill and improving extreme-weather prediction.

items.title: AI-assisted math advance highlights gap between finding answers and judging their significance
items.excerpt: Princeton researchers paired a reasoning model with a coding agent to tighten bounds on the Grothendieck constant, but the system stalled until humans reframed the question.

items.title: Tracking down cellular gene functions with AI and microscopy
items.excerpt: LMU Munich's AI screened microscopy images of ~70 million cells for visual changes caused by gene edits, recovering known autophagy regulators and flagging new candidate genes.

items.title: As AI Closed In on 'Unique Games' Proof, Researchers Raced to Beat the Machines
items.excerpt: In the shadow of a rumored AI proof of one of the biggest problems in their field, three computer scientists rushed to publish their own milestone result.

items.title: Chemical foundation models reveal molecular principles underlying glycobiology
items.excerpt: IBM Research and Trinity College Dublin show that atom-level representations learned by general chemistry foundation models transfer to glycobiology benchmarks spanning taxonomy, immunogenicity and protein-glycan interactions.

items.title: Could AI Face Recognition Falsely ID You?
items.excerpt: A psychologist examines how human and AI face-recognition errors compound when police compare everyday photos against criminal databases.
